title: Contract Paralegal
description:

£26,500.

Central Bristol, no car parking

title: Service Coordinator - Mental Health
description:
We are looking for an experienced and compassionate leader to join our Mental Health Services as a Peripatetic Service Coordinator, supporting teams across Bristol and South Gloucestershire.

What does "Peripatetic" mean for this role?

In this position, "peripatetic" means you will provide cover across our different regional sites, rather than being based permanently at a single location. However, you will not be traveling to a different site every day. You will typically be assigned to one specific project or location for extended periods-often weeks or months at a time-to provide stable, ongoing support where it is needed most.

An exciting pathway to permanence:

Because you will become embedded within the teams you support, this role offers a genuine opportunity to move into a permanent Service Coordinator position should a suitable vacancy arise and align with your skills, experience and success in the role.

About the role

This is an exciting opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of people with complex mental health needs while leading and developing high-performing teams.

As a Service Coordinator, you will lead teams to deliver person-centred support that enables people to achieve their goals, build independence, and gain the skills and confidence to live fulfilling lives in their communities. You will support individuals to build resilience, develop practical life skills, strengthen community connections, and take greater control of their future.

You will be an inspiring and supportive leader with excellent communication and listening skills, able to motivate, develop, and empower colleagues to deliver outstanding support. A strong understanding of person-centred practice and a commitment to promoting positive mental health, wellbeing, and recovery-focused support are essential.

You will ensure services are delivered safely, effectively, and in line with relevant legislation, regulations, and organisational standards, while demonstrating positive outcomes for the people we support.

Travel & Vehicle Requirements

You must have access to your own reliable vehicle for business use. We fully understand that travel is a key part of this role, which is why all business mileage is reimbursed at our standard company rate.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing the day-to-day operation of services, including rota planning and resource allocation, to ensure people receive the right support at the right time.
- Supporting teams to co-produce and regularly review support plans, risk assessments and positive risk management strategies.
- Providing regular supervision, coaching and performance support to team members, while ensuring training and development needs are met.
- Contributing to referrals, assessments and service transition planning.
- Monitoring service budgets and expenditure in line with organisational expectations.
- Providing direct, hands-on support when required and leading by example in delivering high-quality care and support.

About you

The successful candidate will:
- Demonstrate strong leadership skills, with experience of supervising, leading or coordinating a team.
- Be highly organised and able to prioritise competing demands in a fast-paced environment.
- Have experience supporting people with complex mental health needs and a sound understanding of recovery-focused practice.
- Be confident in responding to people who are experiencing acute mental illness, in dynamic risk management and developing escalation plans to ensure that people receive the support that they need.
- Have knowledge of mental health services, legislation and best practice, including experience of trauma-informed approaches.
- Be flexible to work across a seven-day service, including a variety of shift patterns as required.

Why join us?

This is an excellent opportunity to work across a variety of services, develop talented teams and play a key role in shaping high-quality mental health support across Bristol and South Gloucestershire. You'll be joining an organisation that is committed to empowering people, investing in its workforce and continually improving the services it delivers.

At Milestones Trust we recognise that without the hard work, commitment and passion of our staff, we wouldn't be the charity that we are today. In return, we are committed to rewarding you with a competitive pay and benefits package including:
- 34 days' annual leave, including recognised public holidays
- Learning and development to support your career growth
- Nationally recognised qualifications, from entry level care to management
- Flexible working, with rotas provided in advance
- Occupational Sick Pay after two years, increasing with service
- Health Cash Plan after probation, offering at least £695 cashback for health treatments (dental, optical, therapies, maternity/paternity, prescriptions)
- Enhanced maternity and paternity pay
- Free enhanced DBS check
- Dayforce Wallet, giving you access to your earnings before payday
- Employee referral scheme with financial rewards
- Employee Assistance Programme from day one, offering confidential 24/7 support
- Company pension scheme to help grow your retirement savings

We pride ourselves with being able to offer staff opportunities to develop and progress their careers within the Trust.

title: Finance Billing Coordinator
description:
About the role

Are you an organised and detail-focused finance professional who enjoys solving problems and making sure things are done accurately and on time?

We're looking for a Finance Billing Coordinator to join our Finance team and play an important role in ensuring Hft's income is billed accurately, submitted on time and collected efficiently.

The role has a particular focus on Housing billing, while also providing wider support to our Management Accounting team with billing queries, income processes and month-end activities.

You'll work closely with colleagues across Finance and Operations, as well as external stakeholders including Local Authorities, funders and families. You'll need to be confident managing regular deadlines, investigating discrepancies and resolving billing issues, while maintaining excellent attention to detail.

This is a great opportunity for someone with experience in finance, billing, accounts receivable or finance administration who wants to develop their skills within a supportive and collaborative Finance team.

What you'll be doing

You'll take responsibility for a range of billing and income activities, including:
- Coordinating regular Housing billing processes and ensuring invoices are accurate, complete and issued on time.
- Preparing and processing invoices and credit notes.
- Processing changes to customer and tenancy information and billing requirements.
- Submitting invoices to Local Authorities, funders and other customers through relevant systems and portals.
- Monitoring rejected, disputed and unpaid invoices and following up to ensure issues are resolved.
- Responding to billing and income queries from Finance, Operations and external stakeholders.
- Investigating discrepancies, missing information and changes to care or housing arrangements.
- Supporting the Management Accounting team with month-end income activities, including Housing income accruals and deferrals.
- Completing relevant reconciliations and financial checks.
- Providing information and supporting documentation for financial reporting and audit.
- Maintaining accurate records and a clear audit trail.
- Identifying opportunities to improve billing processes, systems and ways of working.
- Providing wider support to the Finance team during busy periods.

What you'll bring

We're looking for someone who is:
- Experienced in a finance, billing, accounts receivable or finance administration environment.
- Comfortable processing invoices, credit notes and other financial transactions.
- Confident dealing with queries and working with both internal and external stakeholders.
- Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Confident using Microsoft Excel and standard Microsoft Office applications.
- Comfortable investigating discrepancies and taking ownership of resolving problems.
- A clear and professional communicator.
- Able to work independently while also being a collaborative member of the wider team.
- Committed to accuracy, financial controls and meeting deadlines.

Experience of working with Local Authorities, funders, Housing or care-related billing would be desirable, as would experience using finance systems, billing platforms or online portals. An AAT or relevant finance qualification would also be advantageous.

Why join Hft?

At Hft, our mission is simple: the best life possible.

We believe people with learning disabilities should be able to live within their communities, with all the choice and support they need to live the best life possible.

As part of our Finance team, you'll play an important role behind the scenes, helping ensure our services have the financial support they need to make this happen.

We're looking for someone who shares our commitment to getting things right, working collaboratively and continually looking for better ways of doing things.

Working arrangements

This is a full-time, permanent hybrid role based in Bristol.

You will be required to work from our Bristol office at least one day each week, with the remainder of your working week carried out from home.

Please ensure you are able to meet this minimum weekly office attendance requirement before applying.

Recruitment process

The closing date for applications is 30 September 2026.

Our recruitment process will consist of one interview stage, which will be held virtually via Microsoft Teams.

If you're looking for your next finance opportunity and would like to make a meaningful contribution as part of a collaborative team, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Technical Claims Handler
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new firm

Our client is a highly respected UK law firm with a well-established insurance practice and a growing delegated claims handling service. Based in the firm's Bristol office, the team manages claims on an outsourced basis for a broad range of leading insurers, underwriting businesses and insurance organisations.

Operating under delegated authority, the team reviews, adjusts and settles claims from first notification through to resolution. Its work focuses on financial loss claims made against professionals, including professional indemnity, title indemnity, technology and media matters. The team does not handle consumer, retail or personal injury claims.

The wider claims function is structured across scheme managers, technical claims handlers, senior claims handlers and claims handlers. Each client is supported by a dedicated scheme manager and claims team, with individuals typically working across more than one client or scheme. This role will be based in the firm's Bristol office, with occasional travel to London where required.

Your new role

This opportunity is available on either a permanent or a 9 month fixed-term contract basis, offering flexibility depending on your preference and circumstances.

An excellent opportunity to join a specialist and growing team, managing a reduced caseload of complex professional indemnity claims while providing technical support, coaching and guidance to colleagues. You'll work closely with insurers, scheme managers and stakeholders to deliver high-quality claims handling and strategic decision-making.
Key responsibilities:
- Manage complex professional indemnity claims from notification to resolution.
- Assess policy coverage, liability, quantum and insurer exposure.
- Investigate claims, develop strategies and make decisions within delegated authority.
- Negotiate settlements and provide accurate insurer reporting.
- Manage external legal providers where required.
- Support, mentor and train claims colleagues.
- Build strong relationships with insurers, brokers, insureds and stakeholders.
- Ensure compliance with SLAs, KPIs and reserving requirements.
- Maintain accurate records on the case management system.

What you'll need to succeed

You will have strong technical claims handling experience and a sound understanding of insurance principles, policy coverage and delegated authority arrangements.
